pass_meta.suite: Global Search V2 - V1 regression set (section 6769)
pass_meta.how_judged: Every verdict is read from the RENDERED ROWS, using the app's own result-row test ids, with the tab strip's counts, the modal's own result-count line and the /api/search response the page was rendered from all required to agree. Zeros are checked against the seed manifest so a missing record is never reported as a product fault.
pass_meta._note: DRAFT - cases still being observed carry no entry yet. make_results.py refuses to emit while any executed case is unjudged.

C45155.observed: The group of vehicles is labelled 'Assets' on the tab strip and on the group heading. The internal word 'Vehicles' is not shown to the user anywhere in the search results.

C45157.observed: Searching 'Kestrel' returned three results and each was a different record - the customer, the part and the supplier. No record was listed twice, even though the word appears in more than one of its fields.

C45161.observed: Typing a single letter ran no search: the panel showed the recently-viewed list instead. Typing two letters ran the search and returned results across five types. Matching begins at two characters, as expected.

C53578.observed: Typing the customer's name returned that customer's four jobs under the Work orders heading. No job number had to be known.

C53579.observed: All four ways of writing the job number found the same job: with a dash, run together, with the shop number in front, and the shop number without the letter. None returned 'no results'.

C53580.observed: Typing the vehicle's unit number returned that vehicle under the Assets heading, and its four jobs alongside.

C53581.observed: Typing the customer's name returned that customer's vehicle under the Assets heading.

C53584.observed: Typing the supplier's email address returned that supplier under the Vendors heading, shown as a contact match.

C53602.observed: Typing the customer's name with all the spaces removed returned that customer under the Customers heading, together with its jobs and its vehicle.

C53607.observed: Typing a word from the part's description returned that part under the Parts heading, and typing two words of the description returned it among the matching parts. A part can be found by its description, not only by its number.

C55659.observed: Typing only part of a number found the record every time: part of the job number found the job, part of the part number found the part, and part of the unit number found the vehicle.

C55661.observed: Searching a word that matches five different kinds of record showed all five on the combined view - the jobs, the customer, the vehicle, the part and the supplier. Nothing that matched was squeezed out.

C55667.observed: Typing part of the company name returned the customer, and typing the full company name returned it again. This is the control the other customer checks depend on, and it holds.

C45156.observed: With the search panel closed, pressing the keyboard shortcut opened it and put the cursor straight in the search box, ready to type.

C45158.observed: Search was present and working on a normal screen with no setting switched on and nothing enabled beforehand - it returned results immediately.

C55683.observed: On a full-size screen the search box shows the shortcut written in it, and hovering explains what it does. On the narrower tablet and phone widths the shortcut is not shown, which is right - there is no keyboard to press it on.

C53583.observed: Typing the customer's website address returned nothing at all, although the customer's record does hold that website.
C53583.todo: The case says to hold this rather than treat it as a fault: the new specification leaves the website out of what a customer can be found by, so this may be a deliberate decision. It needs the Product Owner to say whether searching by website should still work.

C53603.observed: Typing the contact's job title returned nothing. The contact does exist on the customer and does carry that exact job title, so the record is there and the search does not reach it.
C53603.todo: The case says to hold this for the Product Owner: the new specification lists a contact's name, phone and email as searchable but not their job title, so this may be a deliberate decision.

C53601.observed: Neither the part's own number nor a word from its name returned the catalogue part. It is a part that has never been stocked, and it cannot be found at all.
C53601.todo: The case says to hold this for the Product Owner rather than treat it as a fault. It is the change a customer is most likely to notice, because in the previous version every catalogue part could be searched whether or not it had ever been in stock.

C55658.observed: Typing a job status did not return the jobs in that status. Typing 'Estimate' returned one job that is marked Paid, matched on other words on the record, and typing a two-word status run together returned nothing.
C55658.todo: The case says to mark this held and flag it: being able to type a status was how a dispatcher pulled up all the estimates, so the Product Owner needs to decide whether that should come back.

C55660.observed: A fragment from the middle of the city name returned nothing, while fragments from the middle of the company name and of the address both found the customer. So mid-word matching works in some places and not others.
C55660.todo: The case says to mark this held and flag it. The Product Owner needs to decide whether typing a fragment from the middle of any word should find the record, as it did in the previous version.

C55665.observed: No part sale exists to search for. Part sales cannot be created on this branch at present, so the check could not be carried out.
C55665.todo: A part sale needs to be creatable on this branch before this can be run. Once one exists, search the customer's name and look under the Part sales heading.

C55666.observed: Both the part number written with dashes and the same number run together returned the part under the Parts heading. IMPORTANT: this case was written expecting to fail on this build, and it now passes - the part number works both ways.

C55668.observed: Typing just the supplier's first word returned it under the Vendors heading in its own right, even though that word also appears on a part and inside the customer's address. Typing the supplier's full name returned it on its own.

C55670.observed: Typing the contact's first name returned the company, and typing the surname returned it again - both marked as a contact match. Someone who only knows who they speak to can still find the company.

C55672.observed: Typing the bare job number with no prefix returned that job under the Work orders heading.

C55675.observed: A search for a made-up reference showed a clear 'No results found' message. The list did not sit empty, keep spinning, or go on showing the previous results.

C45154.observed: Opening a different record did navigate, which proves the check works. Selecting the record already on screen did not navigate and did not reload the page, and the recently-viewed list was identical before and after - the record was not pushed back to the top.

C53588.observed: Among the four jobs that match equally and share a status, the three nobody had opened appear most-recently-started first. The one listed above them is the job opened a few minutes earlier, which the case names as a signal that rightly outranks recency.
C53588.not_observed: These jobs carry a start time but no separate last-changed time, so the order was judged against when each was started. None had been edited since.

C53586.observed: A new customer was created and then searched for without reloading or signing out. It came back after 17 seconds, inside the 30 seconds allowed.
C53586.not_observed: The record was created through the back end rather than through the screen, so the part of the check about it appearing in the recently-viewed list was not exercised fairly and is not being claimed either way.

C55669.observed: The full chassis number returned the vehicle. The last six characters of it returned nothing. Someone reading the short code off a windscreen plate cannot find the vehicle.
C55669.todo: The case says to hold this for the Product Owner rather than treat it as a fault: matching part of a chassis number was possible in the previous version. Also worth telling him the case is now out of date - it was written expecting the opposite problem, the whole number failing and the front part working, and the behaviour has since changed.

C45153.observed: Every kind of record that could be tested opened the right page: a job opened that job, a customer opened that customer's jobs, a vehicle opened that vehicle's jobs under the right owner, a supplier opened the supplier, and a part opened the stock list for that part. The two that matter most to this case could not be tested - the catalogue-only part cannot be found at all, so there is no row to click, and no part sale exists to click either.
C45153.todo: This needs the catalogue-only part to be findable and a part sale to exist. The catalogue part is the whole point of the case: the previous version opened the catalogue page, and the case exists to check the new version opens something a person can actually use.

C53582.observed: Searching the street, the town and the state each returned the customer. Searching its postcode returned nothing at all, although the customer's record does hold that postcode.
C53582.todo: The case says to hold a postcode miss rather than treat it as a fault: the postcode worked in the previous version but is not in the new specification's list, so the Product Owner needs to decide whether searching by postcode should still work. Worth knowing that the town and the state DO work, so this is specific to the postcode.

C53585.observed: Searching the street and the town each returned the supplier. Searching its postcode returned nothing, although the supplier's record does hold that postcode.
C53585.todo: Same decision as the customer postcode: it worked in the previous version and is not in the new specification's list, so the Product Owner needs to say whether it should still work.

C53604.observed: Searching the customer's second address line returned that customer under the Customers heading. It had returned nothing before the value was actually put on the record - the record had been left empty.
C53604.not_observed: The supplier half is being run separately: no supplier in the test data had a second address line, so a value had to be put on one first.

C55662.observed: Searching the company's own phone number returned nothing, in the formatted version and as plain digits. The number was put onto the record in the same save as the state, and searching the state DOES now find the customer - so the save worked and the search has caught up. The company's phone number simply is not searchable.
C55662.todo: The case says to hold this and flag it. In the previous version a company could be found by its own switchboard number, separately from its contacts' numbers, so the Product Owner needs to decide whether that should come back.

C53606.observed: Searching the state returned one supplier, but not the seeded one - it matched on a name that happens to contain the word. The seeded supplier's record does hold that state and it was not returned.
C53606.todo: The case says to hold this for the Product Owner: the new specification lists a supplier's name, phone, email, street and town as searchable, but not the state.

C55671.observed: All three ways of typing the name - all lower case, all capitals, and a jumble of both - returned exactly the same seven customers, the seeded one among them. Capitals make no difference.

C53516.observed: Searching the vehicle's number plate returned nothing at all - not one result of any kind. The vehicle's record does hold that plate; it was read back off the record to be sure.
C53516.todo: The case says to hold this rather than treat it as a fault: the number plate was searchable in the previous version, and the new specification does not list it among the things a vehicle can be found by. The Product Owner needs to decide whether it should still work. Worth saying plainly what it costs if it does not - the plate is often the only thing written down when a vehicle is booked in.

C55674.observed: Search was reached from the header and found the customer at a full desktop size, at tablet width and at phone width. Nothing had to be tapped open first at any size.
C55674.not_observed: At the two narrower sizes the row of section names does not show its counts. That is a layout difference, not a fault, and the results themselves were all there.

C55680.observed: Arrowing down twelve times and back up six only ever landed on result rows. The headings that separate the sections - Customers, Assets, Vendors and the rest - were stepped over every time, going down and coming back, so the highlight never sat on something that cannot be opened.
